This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 20.12.2022 at about 6.50 a.m. he had been proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-6632 being ridden by his friend one Gajendra near Nidavanda Railway Gate, Dasenahalli Road, Sompura H. Nelamangala,
Bengaluru District, at that time, a rider of another motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-U-9771 came at very high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motor cycle of the petitioner,
due to the tremendous impact, he fell down and sustained injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
he was rushed to Government Hospital for first aid, thereafter shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient and towards medical expenses, he has spent an amount of Rs.2,50,000/-.

entities.text: Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: SCCH-5 3.

Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 42 years, working as security guard,
thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to continue his work, completely bed ridden and has loss his income.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-U-9771 and Dabaspet Police have registered a case in crime No.267/2022 for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

The 1st Respondent being the R.C.Owner and 2nd Respondent being the insurer of the offending motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1/owner has appeared before the tribunal SCCH-5 through his counsel, but not chosen to file written statement.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared before the tribunal through counsel and filed written statement by denying entire averments of the petition.
There is no compliance of Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further denied age,
occupation, income of the petitioner, occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 20.12.2022 at about 6.50 a.m. when petitioner was pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA- 6632 near Nidavanda Railway Gate, Nidavanda-Dasenahalli Road, Sompura, H.Nelamangala, at that time, rider of the another motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-U-9771 drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the claimant motor cycle, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.Vivekananda SCCH-5 B.R. Asst. Professor at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics as PW-2 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21 and closed his evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner inorder to prove his case, he himself examined as PW-1 and in his chief- examination evidence, he has reiterated petition averments.
Though he has been elaborately cross- SCCH-5 examined by the Respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve Ramalingaiah vs Mr. Ravikumar.

10. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked copy of FIR and complaint marked as Ex.P.1, copy of spot mahazar marked as Ex.P.2, copy of IMV Report marked as Ex.P.3, copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet marked as Ex.P.5.
11.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement by respondent No.2, respondents have not SCCH-5 taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 20.12.2022 at about 6.50 a.m. when he was travelling as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HA-6632 near Nidavanda Railway Gate, Dasenahalli Road,
Sompura H. Nelmangala, Bengaluru District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-U-9771.

Under such SCCH-5 circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained right proximal 1/3rd both bone leg fracture, for which he underwent surgery in the form of wound debridement with Ex-fix application.

To prove the nature of the injuries sustained and treatment taken by him, he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.4, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 20.12.2022 to 28.12.2022, further he took treatment from 07.03.2023 to 20.03.2023, thereafter SCCH-5 from 02.05.2023 to 23.05.2023, totally for 42 days.

medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.10, CT- Scan report marked as Ex.P.11, X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.12, CT-Scan films marked as Ex.P.13, OPD Card marked as Ex.P.15, Lab Report marked as Ex.P.16, 4 photographs with CD marked as Ex.P.17 and medical bills to the tune of Rs.5,644/-.

for right lower limb and 29% for whole body.
In cross-examination PW-2 has categorically admitted that, while treating any patient in their hospital, they will provide discount in bills those who have BPL cards and government schemes.

Further deposed that, petitioner got the Chief Minister Relief Ramalingaiah vs Mr. Ravikumar.M Alias Rajakumar.M on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114298113/

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 29% i.e., 1/3rd to the whole SCCH-5 body out of 87% for right lower limb disability, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

15. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 42 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.6 wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 01.01.1970 and the alleged accident is occurred on 20.12.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.6 his age is considered about 53 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 11 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 16. As per his case, he was working as Security Guard, thereby earning Rs.20,000/- p.m., to prove the said fact, he has furnished payslip issued by Sri Vinayaka Enterprises marked as Ex.P.14 for the month SCCH-5 of September 2022, October 2022 and November 2022 in which it is mentioned that net salary of the petitioner is Rs.10,682/-, Rs.14,235/- and Rs. 11,091/- respectively.

On perusal of the payslips placed by the petitioner as per Ex.P.14 there is inconsistency in salary i.e., he got Rs.10,682/- in the month of September 2022, Rs.14,235/- in the month of October 2022 and Rs.11,091/- in the month of November 2022, so there is no fixed salary.
In order to avoid the said confusion, average salary of Rs.12,000/- is considered as notional income for award of compensation in this case.

It is admitted fact that, he took treatment as inpatient at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and SCCH-5 Orthopaedics from 20.12.2022 to 28.12.2022, further he took treatment from 07.03.2023 to 20.03.2023, thereafter from 02.05.2023 to 23.05.2023, totally for 42 days.

sentences.text: For the said period he is entitled for the loss of income as per the notional income of the petitioner should be taken into consideration i.e., Rs.12,000/- p.m.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the income of said quantum for the period he was admitted as inpatient in the hospital.

So petitioner is entitled for Rs.16,800/- towards loss on income during laid up period.
18.
Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.9 medical bills for Rs.73,932/- and Ex.P.18 are the medical bills to the tune of Rs.5,644/-, totally a sum of Rs.79,576/-.

On perusal of the said bills marked as Ex.P.9, Sl.No.31 to 38 are bills issued by Sri Vinayaka Tours and Travels i.e., drop and pick up to Sanjay SCCH-5 Gandhi Hospital for Rs.2,640/- each, totally Rs.21,120/-.
The said travel bills is reduced to the extent of Rs.10,000/-, so that, petitioner is entitled for Rs.11,120/- towards travel bills.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.79,576/- and travel bills of Rs.11,120/-, totally amounting to Rs.90,696/- towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: Further on perusal of Ex.P.4 copy of wound certificate, in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries out of the accident caused on 20.12.2022.
So as per Ex.P.4 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained right leg both bones upper 1/3rd fracture which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Ravikumar @ Ravikumar M. for the offences punishable SCCH-5 under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 clearly states that,
petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.90,696/-.
20.

Further during the course of arguments, respondent No.2 counsel Smt.GR vehemently argued that, this is a case of head on collusion and there is 2 days delay in lodging the complaint and PW-1 in cross- examination categorically admitted about moving of vehicles on left side and right side and she also argued that, as per Ex.P.3 IMV Report, the front portion of the vehicle has been damaged and rider of the vehicle has not been arrayed in this case and this accident was held in between two vehicles i.e., two wheelers and PW-2 SCCH-5 Doctor has categorically admitted the case of respondent and PW-1 chief-examination is contradictory to the medical bills and as per the admissions of the PW-2, entire benefits has been extended to the petitioner.
21.

Per contra, petitioner counsel resisted to the said arguments and argued that, PW-2 Doctor supports the case of the petitioner and 29% whole body disability is given and medical bills is also marked and petitioner is doing security guard work and prays to award the compensation.

22. Considering the nature of the injuries, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.15,000/-
towards pain and sufferings.
The Petitioner was treated as inpatient for a period of 42 days Sanjay Gandhi Hospital.
Considering the duration of treatment, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards conveyance, nourishment and SCCH-5 attendant charges.

Considering the fracture injury sustained by the petitioner and disability as stated by the Doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of amenities.
23.

Per contra except denial in the written statement and oral evidence, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case,
because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
SCCH-5 24.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,11,856/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.
26. Though the Respondent No.2 has taken several defence in its written statement, but whatever defence taken is not at all established except by leading evidence.
SCCH-5
In other words, the respondents have not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner.

The Respondent No.2 in its written statement admits that, it has issued policy with respect to motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-U-9771 vide policy No.2312910182201700000 for the period from 28.05.2022 to 27.05.2027, the alleged accident was occurred on 20.12.2022.

Therefore,
as on the date of accident, the insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as discussed above, the insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident.
hence the respondent No.2 Insurance Company shall deposit above said compensation amount SCCH-5 with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

27. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,11,856/- (Rupees Six Lakhs Eleven Thousand Eight Hundred Fifty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof Ramalingaiah vs Mr. Ravikumar.M Alias Rajakumar.M on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114298113/
